Here is a simple project in PyGame that includes keyboard event handling and an FPS counter in the top left corner of the window:

```python
import pygame
import sys
import time
import random

pygame.init()

# Set up the display
width, height = 800, 600
display = pygame.display.set_mode((width, height))
pygame.display.set_caption("Simple PyGame Project")

# Set up the clock
clock = pygame.time.Clock()

# Set up the FPS counter
font = pygame.font.Font(None, 36)
fps_text = font.render("FPS: 0", True, (0, 0, 0))

# Main game loop
running = True
while running:
    # Event handling
    for event in pygame.event.get():
        if event.type == pygame.QUIT:
            running = False
        if event.type == pygame.KEYDOWN:
            if event.key == pygame.K_ESCAPE:
                running = False

    # Update the FPS counter
    fps = clock.get_fps()
    fps_text = font.render(f"FPS: {int(fps)}", True, (0, 0, 0))

    # Fill the display
    display.fill((255, 255, 255))

    # Draw the FPS counter
    display.blit(fps_text, (10, 10))

    # Update the display
    pygame.display.flip()

    # Cap the frame rate
    clock.tick(60)

# Quit the game
pygame.quit()
sys.exit()
```

This example creates a window with a white background and a black FPS counter in the top left corner. The game loop checks for keyboard events and updates the FPS counter every frame. The game will quit when the user presses the ESC key.
